svg.title: France wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Follow the Atlantic west, continental northeast and Mediterranean south through nine established study groupings. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Champagne. Northeastern France, around Reims and Épernay; north of Burgundy. 2: Alsace. Eastern France, between the Vosges foothills and the Rhine plain. 3: Loire Valley. A long west–east corridor. These middle and upper Loire locators do not imply one compact vineyard zone. 4: Burgundy. East-central France; the representative Côte d’Or location does not cover all Burgundy vineyards. 5: Beaujolais. South of the Mâconnais and north of Lyon. 6: Rhône Valley. Two locators distinguish the narrow northern corridor from the broader southern vineyards. 7: Provence. Mediterranean southeastern France, east of the lower Rhône. 8: Bordeaux. Southwestern France around the Gironde estuary and adjoining river valleys. 9: Languedoc-Roussillon. Mediterranean arc west of the Rhône; Roussillon lies nearer the Spanish border.

g.text: Dots locate representative places · boundaries do not represent appellations
